أَعْيَسُ A camel of a white colour mixed with somewhat of [the red hue termed] شُقْرَة; (S, O, K; *) [i. e., reddish white] or [dingy white;] white with a slight darkness (Msb:) or inclining to yellow: [i. e., yellowish white:] (I Aar:) fem. عَيْسَآءُ: pl. عِيسٌ: (S, O, Msb, K:) the camels thus termed are said to be of good breed. (S, O,) Also A gazelle, or an antelope, and a bull, [app. meaning a wild bull,] in which is [a hue such as is termed] أَدْمَة. (TA.) And you say رَجُلٌ أَعْيَسُ الشَّعَرِ A man having white hair. (TA.) And رَسْمٌ أَعْيَسُ A white mark, trace, relic, or remain. (TA.) ―
-b2- العَيْسَآءُ The female locust. (S, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
